fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the access drive so responders can identify the property quickly from the roadway.
• Mark the circular driveway's entry and exit points with reflective posts so responders can identify the correct flow of travel under low-visibility conditions.
• Trim vegetation along the edges of the access drive to maintain clear vehicle clearance for fire apparatus and other large emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the main residence to keep walking paths clear for responders moving around the structure on foot.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of parked cars along the path between the access drive and the main entrance so responding units have a direct route to the front door.
• Post a visible marker or sign at each secondary access point so responders can locate alternate routes to the residence without searching through dense vegetation.
• Trim shrubs and low tree branches along walkways so responders carrying equipment can move between the parking area and the residence without obstruction.
• Thin dense vegetation near the circular driveway to allow multiple units to stage simultaneously without blocked sightlines between crews.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters near structures to create more open space between the trees and the buildings.
• Remove low-hanging branches from trees within the clusters closest to the structures.
• Keep grass areas around structures mowed short to reduce the amount of burnable material on the ground.
• Separate any tree clusters that are close enough to touch or overlap each other with the structures caught in between.
• Maintain the open green space areas by keeping them free of dead leaves, fallen branches, and other dry material.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can move through without obstruction.
• Trim scattered trees so their lower branches do not connect ground-level grass to the upper canopy.
• Keep the areas under tree clusters clear of accumulated dead leaves, sticks, and dry debris.
